compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`enrich_drain._spawn_detached_drain` starts the detached drain child with
`subprocess.Popen([...], env=..., stdin=..., stdout=..., stderr=log_fh, **_detach_kwargs())` —
with **no `cwd=`**. The child therefore inherits the parent's working directory.

rebar's own workflow creates short-lived worktrees and removes them (`make worktree` /
`git worktree remove`). When a write from inside such a worktree spawns a drain child and the
worktree is later removed, the child's inherited cwd no longer exists. `queue.claim` calls
`_tracker(repo_root)` -> `config.tracker_dir` -> `_config_sources.repo_root` -> `Path.cwd()`,
and `os.getcwd()` raises:

```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

The drain aborts before claiming anything.

## Evidence (2026-08-20, this repo's own store)

`.rebar/logs/enrich-drain.log` carries this traceback for **four distinct removed worktrees**:

```
/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-ci-latency-debug
/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-debug-structured-duplicates
/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-debug-zizmor-online
/Users/joeoakhart/split-config-writer
```

The store currently holds **3 permanently pending enrichment entries** that never drain:

```
8625-7bea-67db-4cdc   9305-b42c-3262-4c58   e27c-5a20-cd13-43b2
```

Notably these are also the three largest ticket directories in the store (870 / 747 / 621
event files) — the most re-certified tickets, so the ones most often re-enqueued.

## Why this matters beyond a failed drain

It defeats the fix for `moist-short-lionfish` (958e-f4b3-275c-4154). That bug makes the
write-path drain gate O(1) via a marker recording "nothing can be pending before T". The fast
path is only reachable when the queue is genuinely quiet — correctly so, since a marker must
never be able to hide real work. With entries wedged pending forever, the gate keeps doing the
full O(ticket-count) store walk on every write and the 20 ms budget warning keeps firing, even
with 958e landed. So 958e's acceptance criterion "the WARNING no longer fires on an ordinary
write" is not observable on this store until this is fixed.

## Approach (to be confirmed by whoever claims this)

Pass an explicit, known-good `cwd` to the detached child rather than inheriting one that may be
gone — the tracker's parent (the repo root) is already computed by `_rebar_dir(tracker)` and is
the natural choice. Consider also whether `_config_sources.repo_root`'s `Path.cwd()` fallback
should degrade rather than raise, since any detached/daemonised caller has the same exposure.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` (`_spawn_detached_drain`)
- possibly `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` (`repo_root`'s cwd fallback)
- tests under `tests/unit/`

## Testing
- A test that spawns the drain child from a directory that is removed before the child resolves
  the tracker, and asserts the drain still claims and processes the entry.
- A test pinning that the child is launched with an explicit `cwd` that does not depend on the
  caller's.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A detached drain child started from a since-removed worktree still resolves the tracker
      and drains.
- [ ] The three wedged entries above drain (or an equivalent reproduction does).
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and CI's pytest invocation are green.

## Provenance
Found while debugging 958e-f4b3-275c-4154 (moist-short-lionfish) — the reason that bug's fix
cannot be observed end-to-end on this store. Out of that ticket's scope (different file,
different mechanism), filed rather than folded in.
compiled_state.title: detached drain child inherits a removed worktree's cwd and dies at getcwd()
